premises.statement: A part is ordered to a whole as imperfect to perfect.
An individual person is a part of a complete community.
The city is the complete political community.
Particular commands apply a law whose order remains to common good.
A particular act can refer to common good through a common final cause, not a common genus or species.
Practical reasoning is resolved to its ultimate end.
The objection infers from singular commands that law need not aim at common good.
The objection infers from particular acts that law aims at a particular good.
The objection invokes rational private goods against an exclusively common end.
The sed contra cites law written for common civic utility rather than private advantage.
The respondeo identifies the ultimate end as the first principle in practical matters.
The respondeo identifies happiness or beatitude as the ultimate end of human life.
Cross-referenced prior principle: happiness or beatitude is the ultimate end of human life. This exact premise is imported as an assumption, not a verified lemma.
The respondeo uses a focal analogy in which derivative cases are ordered to the case that is most fully named.
The inference from a person as a part of the complete community to law’s orientation to that community’s happiness is an explicit reconstructed bridge.
